final_recommendation: The room converged on a negotiated settlement: FINMA commits to publishing a comprehensive Friday statement with explicit AT1 seniority restoration, a 45-60% recovery range, a preliminary payout schedule, and unambiguous language limiting the emergency ordinance to Credit Suisse's viability crisis. Bondholder counsel stands down the federal filing for a 60-day window contingent on delivery.
minority_objections: Insurance observer repeatedly warned that D&O/E&O exposure persists for 8+ years regardless of settlement language, as breach-of-fiduciary and negligent-misrepresentation claims against advisers remain viable
Credit market analyst cautioned that trader repricing of peer AT1 (150-200 bps wider) may occur Monday despite FINMA's statement if markets read it as 'FINMA has the power but won't use it'
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel vs. FINMA legal over whether a signed carrier memo would constitute discovery evidence of precedent acknowledgment (R5-R6)
Institutional investors vs. FINMA over whether methodology alone suffices or concrete recovery percentages are required to stop market repricing (R3-R4)
Bondholder group vs. FINMA over whether 'does not establish precedent' language constitutes a liability admission that triggers insurer reserves (R6)
key_concessions: FINMA committed to publishing a 45-60% AT1 recovery range by Friday (R4), a major shift from vague guidance to modelable numbers
FINMA agreed to explicit 'sole purpose' and 'does not authorize' language limiting the ordinance to Credit Suisse viability facts (R8)
FINMA offered a preliminary payout schedule (12% by June 30, 15% by September 30, remainder by end-2024) contingent on UBS/SNB confirmations (R7)
Bondholder counsel withdrew the Monday federal filing threat in exchange for Friday delivery of the comprehensive statement (R8)
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: Friday statement must explicitly rank senior AT1 above common equity in payout waterfall, with published valuation methodology—no buried appendices (R2)
Institutional investors: Recovery framework must include modelable cash flow expectations (range or schedule), not just process—otherwise they assume 20 cents on the dollar (R3-R4)
Bondholder group: FINMA must publish affirmative doctrine statement that AT1 seniority is 'restored and binding across Swiss banking going forward'—not just 'we won't do it again' (R8)
Bondholder counsel: Any softening of 'sole purpose' / 'does not authorize' language or slippage in payout schedule delivery triggers immediate Monday filing (R8)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Multi-year D&O/E&O claims tail against UBS advisers and FINMA officials persists regardless of settlement, as breach-of-fiduciary and negligent-misrepresentation claims remain viable (insurance observer, R7-R8)

Trader repricing of peer AT1 (UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank) may still occur Monday if markets interpret FINMA's statement as preserving latent ordinance authority rather than binding self-limitation (credit analyst, R8)
Discovery risk: FINMA's 'does not establish precedent' language may be cited in future complaints as written acknowledgment that the write-down was legally contestable (bondholder counsel, R6)
downstream_risk_variables: UBS merger close and SNB funding confirmation by Wednesday EOD (required for payout schedule validity)
Carrier counsel sign-off on reserve-closure language by Thursday EOD (affects D&O exposure narrative)
Market interpretation Monday of whether FINMA's 'sole purpose' language constitutes binding self-limitation or merely describes this application
Breadth of federal complaint if filed later: ultra vires only vs. breach-of-fiduciary + negligent-misrepresentation against advisers
Duration and severity of claims tail if litigation proceeds despite settlement (8+ years per insurance observer)
uncertainty_notes: The settlement hinges on FINMA's ability to deliver all components (recovery range, payout schedule, seniority language, ordinance scope limitation) by Friday close. If any element softens or slips, bondholder counsel files Monday. Even if delivered, residual uncertainty remains over: (1) whether traders Monday will reprice peer AT1 despite the statement, (2) whether insurers will close reserves or maintain multi-year D&O exposure, and (3) whether the 'does not establish precedent' language becomes discovery evidence in future litigation.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Federal complaint drafting, unified counsel mandate, and imminent Monday filing threat drove every round (R1-R8); bondholder counsel's withdrawal in R8 was contingent, not unconditional—litigation remained the forcing mechanism throughout
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's legal authority under the emergency ordinance was challenged as ultra vires from R1 onward; the entire negotiation centered on whether FINMA could commit to a recovery framework without parliamentary process, and whether the ordinance itself was legally contestable
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: The inversion of AT1/equity hierarchy was the core grievance driving the room; every concession (tier structure, seniority language, 'sole purpose' limitation) was extracted to address this precedent damage—it shaped the entire settlement structure
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing (150-200 bps wider, 20-30% downside) was discussed as a consequence of precedent uncertainty (R2-R8), but it was secondary to the hierarchy inversion itself—the room focused more on fixing the legal/structural problem than on market mechanics
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Insurance observer raised multi-year D&O/E&O exposure (8+ years) in R5-R8, and bondholder counsel confirmed breach-of-fiduciary claims in R7, but this was a persistent background concern rather than a decision-driving theme—the room prioritized stopping the Monday filing over modeling the tail
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O carrier reserves, insurer sign-off on FINMA's language, and claims against advisers surfaced in R5-R8, but as a secondary consideration—the room debated whether carrier memos would constitute discovery evidence, not whether financial-lines exposure itself was structurally unmanageable
